_note: Owner: P4. ISS vs Mars radiation dose for the 'Where the data comes from' screen. Every number is copied from the linked NASA page (checked 2026-11-15). perDayMSv for the ISS = the six-month numbers divided by 182.5 days.

iss.source: NASA educator guide "Space Faring: The Radiation Challenge" (EP-2008-08-116-MSFC), page 8: crews on the space station receive an average of 80 mSv for a six-month stay at solar maximum and 160 mSv at solar minimum

mars.source: NASA news release, 9 Dec 2013: Curiosity's RAD measured an average of 0.67 millisieverts per day on the surface at Gale Crater (Hassler et al., Science 343, 2014, doi:10.1126/science.1244797)

radlab._note: Raw measurements from NASA RadLab (OSDR), yearly mean of absorbed_dose_rate, converted from uGy/hour to mGy/day. Absorbed dose (mGy), NOT dose equivalent (mSv): per mGy the radiation on Mars is heavier and does more harm, so these numbers must not be compared with the mSv above. Not shown to players; kept for the team.
